headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to prevent large energy users, such as data centers, from shifting their grid infrastructure costs onto residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor Spanberger
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users
news_headline: Power-Bill Fears Drove Virginia's First-In-Nation Data Center Tax
news_summary: Virginia has become the first state to tax data center electricity consumption, imposing a 1.1 cent per kilowatt-hour levy starting July 1, 2026. This move reflects growing public concern that the AI buildout could raise electricity bills for households, challenging the long-held belief that data centers are an automatic economic boon.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates data centers to report their water consumption, providing transparency on their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Be Made Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, with the aggregated numbers to be made publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to increase transparency regarding the significant water consumption by the rapidly growing data center industry in the state.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes regulations for where data centers can be built and sets limits on the noise they produce, addressing community concerns.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry
news_headline: Virginia Residents Take Desperate Measures Against Data Center Noise
news_summary: Residents in Sterling, Virginia, are resorting to extreme measures like installing mattresses and plexiglass in their windows to block the constant humming noise from a nearby data center. This ongoing issue, described as a high-pitched whine from natural gas turbines, significantly impacts their quality of life and has led to numerous complaints.
